91e53285dfee54a08f652a09e3840f60093c7be8.summary: Analysis of Fruitfly, a newly discovered Mac malware family. It conducts surveillance on targeted networks, including capturing screenshots and webcam images and gathering information about devices on the same network. Malwarebytes described it as seemingly targeting biomedical research centers. Its infection route is unclear. Evidence suggests it may have circulated for more than two years, possibly since the Yosemite release of OS X in 2014.

The attacks were underway since at least October 2023 and appear aimed at intelligence gathering. The report says attribution to one specific group cannot be determined. It describes open-source and living-off-the-land tools, keyloggers, login-credential interception through authentication filter DLLs, proxy tools, and archive-based data…

914920782896744cb68f707aefc8173812152684.summary: Group-IB report on Cron, a Russian gang that used Android banking Trojans to steal money from bank customers. The report says the gang infected over 1 million devices via spam SMS links and fake apps, and rented the Tiny.z Trojan in June 2016 to prepare attacks on banks in France and other countries. In November 2016, Russian law enforcement, supported by Group-IB, detained 16 members.
